title: Mature tested subsystem has a credible rewrite path
task: Review a proposal to replace an ad hoc internal scheduler with a new dependency-graph implementation.
context: The current scheduler is behaviorally stable but accumulated years of special cases.
Recorded production fixtures can be replayed through both implementations.
The new design materially simplifies dependency ordering and cycle handling.
A feature flag allows old/new side-by-side comparison and rollback.
evidence: Prototype results match the old implementation across the regression corpus except for documented existing bugs.
The new representation directly models dependencies that are currently encoded through sequencing conventions.
Cutover can be staged and reversed.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Reject the rewrite because rewrites are always dangerous.
Require endless incremental patching because behavior preservation means implementation replacement is forbidden.
expected_decision_properties: Recognize that a rewrite can be credible when behavior is understood and independently testable.
Use the old implementation and replay corpus as behavioral oracles while classifying known bugs explicitly.
Require staged comparison/cutover and rollback rather than trusting structural elegance.
Acknowledge the replacement advantage of directly modeling the dependency graph.
unacceptable_reasoning: A clean data model alone is enough to approve a rewrite.
Old/new differences should all be treated as regressions even when the old behavior is a documented defect.
expected_tradeoffs: replacement risk vs accumulated patch complexity
behavioral compatibility vs intentionally fixing known defects
verification_expectations: Run old/new implementations against the same replay corpus.
Exercise feature-flag rollback and staged cutover.
revisit_when: Side-by-side results reveal unexplained behavioral divergence.
Migration or rollback no longer remains practical.
